name: deadlineread
algorithm: n round trips of one byte over a loopback TCP connection (an echo task, goroutine or thread reads each byte and writes it back; the main one writes i % 251, then reads the echo); sum = 31 sum + the byte read, wrapping; prints n, sum and the failed calls. Variant bare: the read is plain. Variant deadline: each read is bounded by the library's one-operation timeout of one second, which never fires (Mk: a scope of its own with Scope.CancelAfter per read, D8-3; Go: SetReadDeadline per read; Rust: set_read_timeout once, which bounds every later read; C: setsockopt SO_RCVTIMEO once). No cell makes a system call per read for its timeout (README.md). D8-3 (6): Mk's deadline cell is recorded against its bare cell, with its cause (README.md).

skip.zig: not written: Zig 0.17's std.Io stream has no per-read timeout of its own; its form would be a select over the read and a sleep future, which is not one library call as the other cells are

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; sum checks that every read returned the byte written, in order
notes: D8-3 (6)'s second row. Its cause, measured by hand on the owner's machine (Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, other agents running; rt8 session 5, not a tools/bench number): a loopback round trip on IOCP is about 34 microseconds (3,461 ms bare and 3,423 ms with the deadline for 100,000, the best of 5 each), and a deadline scope adds one timer arm and one synchronous disarm on std.task's timer heap, which is below that run's noise.
Checksums from a Go model (sum = 31 sum + i % 251 over 0..n, wrapping) and each column's verify run. The publish size is a guess until tools/bench publish times the row on a quiet machine.
Written by rt8 (plan/08-m8.md 3.3 and section 2's D8-3 (6)); status/rt8.md records what was measured and on what.
